messages.author: 24cd2253f4cae0aa
messages.subject: Windows XP Install Difficulties
parts:
Good Evening:
 
I have read through many of the Windows users who have had Rattle installation problems. I have tried all of the fixes that I found and that seemed to apply to my problems. I have updated all required packages and I have followed, or tried to follow, the internet-connected installation instructions. The results of rattle.info() are shown below.
 
For some reason every time I attempt to launch Rattle with rattle() I am prompted with the Need GTK+?... dialogue box. I have been through so many uninstalls and reinstalls that I have honestly lost count. Once I get through another reinstall I get the same error when trying to launch rattle():
 
In addition: Warning message:
package 'RGtk2' was built under R version 2.12.1
Failed to load RGtk2 dynamic library, attempting to install it.
Learn more about GTK+ at http://www.gtk.org
If the package still does not load, please ensure that GTK+ is installed and that it is on your PATH environment variable
IN ANY CASE, RESTART R BEFORE TRYING TO LOAD THE PACKAGE AGAIN
Error in as.GType(type) : Cannot convert RGtkBuilder to GType
 
I have, by the way, attempted to rememedy the problem by restarting R but this seems to have no effect. I have also uninstalled and reinstalled gtk-2.12.9-win32-2.exe and gtk2-runtime-2.22.0-2010-10-21-ash.exe many times also with no success.
 
Here is my rattle.info() output:

Oddly enough, I attempted the install on a Vista machine. Unfortunately, the Vista machine is not my primary computer and I do need to get the package installed on this XP machine.
 
Any help would be appreciated.
 
And Merry Christmas by the way since I just noticed that it is actually 25 Dec.

messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: Re: Windows XP Install Difficulties
parts:
Hi Adam,

I think the key here is that you may have two versions of GTK interfering with each  other. Essentially, never install gtk 2.12.9 (nor any other version other than 2.22.0) and make sure every incarnation of it is removed from the computer and do some file searching to make sure you can't find any gtk files hanging around. Then install 2.22.0 and the rest.

At least that would be my guess.

Hope that works.

Regards,
Graham

Thanks for taking the time to reply to me. You are indeed correct that two versions of GTK were running. I picked up the odd combination of the two files from another user's solution notes. This step, which seemed to allow Rattle to run on his machine, also resulted in Rattle running successfully on my Vista machine. messages.author: 24cd2253f4cae0aa
messages.subject: Re: Windows XP Install Difficulties
parts:
Hello Shane:
 
Thanks for the reply. I noticed that the PATH on the Vista machine where both Rattle and GGobi work has the following at the beginning: %GTK_BASEPATH%\bin; and then at the end of the PATH is C:\Program Files (x86)\GTK2-Runtime\bin. And of course there is a separate GTK_BASEPATH.
 
I am unfortunately and admittedly not very familiar with editing PATH variables. I assume that the structure on the Vista machine may be part of the solution to the problem on the XP machine, but I have not tried to make the PATH variables similar (less the (x86) portion). I'd be grateful for any advice in this area.
 
I wondered if this was part of the potential fix. I am frankly not sure but I'm willing to try almost anything at this point.
 
A little additional information that developed since my last reply: GGobi is working on the XP machine where I have been trying to get Rattle to work; however, GGobi would not work without the potentially conflicting gtk-2.12.9-win32-2.exe which the GGobi site points users to as a required step in the installation process.
 
Adam

messages.author: 24cd2253f4cae0aa
messages.subject: Resolved Inexplicably: Windows XP Install Difficulties
parts:
I should have examined my PATH variable before my last response to the helpful suggestion from Shane Butler.
 
Both the Vista PATH and the XP PATH are similar and begin with %GTK_BASEPATH%\bin. Both include the approximate same GTK_BASEPATH variable.
 
So, out of frustration and some crazy mix of luck and hope I opened R, executed the library(rattle) command and then rattle(). Once again this generated the Need GTK+?...dialogue box. I almost cancelled but I decided to go through another uninstall/reinstall iteration, then I restarted R. I repeated the library...rattle() commands and to my complete surprise Rattle started.
 
I received prompts for two additional packages:
 
XML, not available via CRAN mirrors but through a net repository using this command:
install.packages("XML", repos = "http://www.omegahat.org/R")
 
cairoDevice, also not available as a Windows binary from a CRAN mirror. I installed via a local zip downloaded from:
http://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/pub/RWin/bin/windows/contrib/2.12/
 
I am perplexed about why Rattle is working, especially because my PATH variables on the XP and Vista machines appear to be the same, and because both machines now contain the potentially conflicting versions of GTK assuming I understand what these two packages are and how they function.
 
I wish I could point to a process that I followed which resulted in a successful Rattle install, but this is the best I can do. I hope the information is helpful.

Shane
